youtube_description:
In 1394 the strongest man in Japan gave up the office of shogun, and a year later he shaved his head and gave up the chancellorship too. Seven years after that, the emperor of China sent a letter calling him 'King of Japan.' In 1408 the emperor of Japan himself came to visit his golden pavilion. If you were the most powerful man in Japan, would you have accepted a title from the emperor of China, or refused it?

📰 Your reporter: Tokio Kamiya, a former Tokyo foreign correspondent. His grandfather's brass pocket watch carries him to one day of Japan's past at a time. He can watch and he can speak, but he can never change what happens. This time he files his dispatch from the road to Kitayama, north of Kyoto, in the spring of 1408, the day the emperor came to visit a monk.

In 1378 he built himself a great residence in Kyoto, the Hana no Gosho, the 'Palace of Flowers.' People say it is why his government is called the Muromachi shogunate. By his thirties he was the strongest man in the capital. Hold on to that, because it makes what he does next so strange.
